contradictions.source: prius igitur occurrit intellectui nostro cognoscere animal et cognoscere homine.
contradictions.english: Therefore, it occurs to our intellect first to know "animal" and to know "man."
contradictions.why: The source says it occurs to the intellect to know animal first, then man; the English implies both occur first simultaneously.

contradictions.source: et quod cognitio singularium est prior quo ad nos et cognitio uniuersalis cognitio sensitiua et cognitio intellectiua. si et sensum et cum intellectu cognitio magis et est prior et cognitio minoris et cois.
contradictions.english: And that the cognition of singulars is prior as to us, and the cognition of universal [is posterior]. Sensitive cognition and intellectual cognition, if it is sense and with intellect, the cognition [of the more] is prior and the cognition of the less and common [is posterior].
contradictions.why: The English text contradicts itself within the same sentence regarding whether the more universal or the less universal is prior.

contradictions.source: et hoc modo magis et est pus et in nam quod apparet manifeste in generatione bo minis et aialis. naz prius generatur animal bo: ut et or in in libro de generatione animalium.
contradictions.english: And in this mode, the more [universal] is prior in nature, which appears manifestly in the generation of man and animal. For the animal is generated before the man, as Aristotle says in the book On the Generation of Animals .
contradictions.why: The source says animal is generated before man; the English swaps the order in the first clause, claiming man is generated before animal.

contradictions.source: sic igitur animal consideratum in se pus et in nostra cognitione et bo. si bo et pus i nra cognitione et animal sic per ronis eius.
contradictions.english: Thus, therefore, animal considered in itself is prior in our cognition, and man [is posterior]. If man [is prior] in our cognition, then animal [is posterior] by its reason.
contradictions.why: The English text asserts that animal is prior in cognition, then immediately asserts the opposite (if man is prior, animal is posterior).
